title: SkyDrive and Suzuki Deepen India eVTOL Push with Kineco Manufacturing Pact
excerpt: Japan's SkyDrive has partnered with Indian composite manufacturer Kineco to build parts for its SD-05 air taxi, adding to Suzuki's growing role in bringing eVTOL technology to Indian cities.
body:
• SkyDrive announced a strategic partnership with India's Kineco Limited at Farnborough Airshow 2026 to manufacture composite aerostructures for the SD-05 eVTOL
  • Suzuki Motor Corporation is SkyDrive's official production partner, with manufacturing underway at a Suzuki plant in Iwata City, Japan
  • India's JetSetGo has pre-ordered 50 SkyDrive eVTOL aircraft for commercial routes starting in Gujarat
  • SkyDrive targets full commercial operations by 2028, with type certification progressing through Japan's JCAB

Farnborough Partnership

SkyDrive Inc., the Japanese eVTOL developer backed by Suzuki Motor Corporation, announced a strategic partnership with India's Kineco Limited at the Farnborough International Airshow 2026, according to Aviation Defence Universe. Under the agreement, Kineco will develop and manufacture high-performance composite aerostructures for SkyDrive's production aircraft, the SD-05.

Production will use Kineco's newly installed 3-meter by 12-meter Scholz Autoclave at its facility in Goa — one of India's largest aerospace composite processing systems. The partnership marks Kineco's first dedicated eVTOL production program.

"This collaboration reflects the shared commitment of India and Japan to advance sustainable aviation technologies, while reinforcing Kineco's capabilities in delivering complex, flight-critical composite aerostructures."

— Vivek Srivastava, Group CEO, Kineco Limited

The Suzuki Connection

Suzuki serves as SkyDrive's official production partner, with manufacturing of the SD-05 prototype already underway at a Suzuki-owned plant in Iwata City, Japan, according to AIN Online. Suzuki has also acted as a broker between SkyDrive and potential customers in India, one of its strongest automotive markets.

The SD-05 is a three-seat eVTOL air taxi designed for routes of up to approximately 50 miles. SkyDrive conducted a successful flight at Expo 2025 Osaka and is currently pursuing type certification from Japan's Civil Aviation Bureau (JCAB), with AutoEvolution reporting that the company is nearing the final phases of the certification process.

SkyDrive is also working concurrently with the FAA for the American market, targeting a 2028 global commercial launch.

India's eVTOL Ambitions

The Kineco deal adds to SkyDrive's growing Indian footprint. In January 2025, JetSetGo, one of India's largest private jet operators, signed a business partnership with SkyDrive and placed a pre-order for 50 eVTOL aircraft. The partnership, facilitated by Suzuki, will initially develop commercial routes around Ahmedabad in Gujarat before expanding to other locations.

"Together, we aim to tackle some of India's pressing mobility-related challenges, including the high level of transport-related emissions and the inefficiencies of urban traffic congestion."

— Tomohiro Fukuzawa, CEO, SkyDrive Inc.

SkyDrive also signed India's Cyient as its first Indian engineering partner for advanced air mobility, covering design and engineering support for the eVTOL program.

Manufacturing in India

The Kineco partnership positions India as a manufacturing node in SkyDrive's global supply chain — a pattern that aligns with India's broader push to become an aerospace manufacturing hub under its 'Make in India' initiative. With Kineco's 30-plus years of composite expertise serving railway, defence, marine, and renewable energy sectors, the company brings established aerospace-grade manufacturing capabilities to the eVTOL sector.

For the Indian aviation industry, the convergence of Japanese eVTOL technology, Suzuki's automotive manufacturing scale, and Indian composite manufacturing could create a new industrial corridor — one that links Goa's aerospace factories to air taxi routes over Ahmedabad's congested streets.
nri_angle: The SkyDrive-Suzuki-India partnership could create new aerospace manufacturing jobs in India and bring air taxi services to congested Indian cities.
